speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; tell me, how long have these symptoms been present, and are the blisters fluid-filled or crusted?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Captopril-induced Stomatitis and Bullous Pemphigoid.

I have already noted your medication history, but please confirm if you have noticed any other skin rashes, such as a rash on your trunk or legs, and whether you have experienced any fever or joint pain recently. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, C3_C4_Complement_Levels, ESR, CRP. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Skin_Biopsy, Oral_Biopsy.
